questions.template: A SMALL gear drives a BIG gear. The big gear turns…?
questions.hint: Big gears have more teeth to click past — that takes time!
questions.explain: Small driving big trades speed for strength: the big gear turns slower but with more force.

questions.template: A see-saw is a simple machine. Which one?
questions.hint: A stiff beam tipping on a middle point…
questions.explain: A see-saw is a lever: a beam balancing on a pivot (the fulcrum). Levers help lift heavy things!

questions.template: Which machine uses a WHEEL and a ROPE to lift things?
questions.hint: Flag poles and cranes use them!
questions.explain: A pulley turns a hard lift into an easy pull — the rope runs over a wheel and changes direction.

questions.template: A {a}-tooth gear drives a {a*3}-tooth gear. How many times does the small one turn for ONE big turn?
questions.hint: Divide the big teeth by the small teeth: {a*3} ÷ {a}.
questions.explain: {a*3} ÷ {a} = 3, so the small gear spins 3 times per big turn — a 3:1 ratio. That's the times tables driving real machines!

questions.template: Two gears mesh together. The first turns clockwise. The second turns…?
questions.hint: Teeth push each other in OPPOSITE directions where they meet.
questions.explain: Meshing gears always swap direction: clockwise drives anticlockwise, tick drives tock.

questions.template: To lift a heavy rock with a lever more easily, push…?
questions.hint: A longer arm means a mightier push!
questions.explain: The further from the fulcrum you push, the more lifting power you get — long levers move mountains (and mine carts).

questions.template: An 8-tooth gear drives a 24-tooth gear. The 24 drives another 8. How fast does the LAST gear spin compared to the first?
questions.hint: ×3 slower, then ×3 faster… what do they make together?
questions.explain: 8→24 divides speed by 3; 24→8 multiplies by 3. They cancel out — the ends match, though the middle turns slowly and strongly.

questions.template: A CAM is a wobbly wheel that turns spinning into…?
questions.hint: Think of an egg-shaped wheel lifting a rod as it turns.
questions.explain: Cams are lumpy wheels: as they spin, their bump pushes a follower up and lets it drop — hello, bouncing toys!

questions.template: In the design loop, what comes right after you BUILD something?
questions.explain: Plan, build, TEST, improve — then loop again. Every great machine failed its first test and got better.
